note: Old coal strip-mine land grown up in woods, managed with the adjoining Harmony Mission Lake area. Two primitive spots, both small gravel pull-offs in dense timber on the area's gravel road: one just inside the Route A entrance, the other about 900 m south near Strip Pit 4. The water-filled pits are 40-60 m away through the trees and not in view. No open fires. No facilities, and the lots are small; spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites' - two mapped Primitive Camping symbols and two GIS points, each at a small gravel lot in woods on the area road. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. No strip pit in view: not waterfront kept. Pin fine. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays): the area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites' and says the areas 'provide recreational opportunities to the public including hunting, trapping and camping'; the brochure: 'Primitive camping is permitted only in designated areas.' The 12/9/2022 map draws a Primitive Camping symbol beside a Parking Lot at two places on the Peabody tract: on the west gravel road just south of Route A (= GIS point 158, the stored pin, 17 m from lot 356) and at the lot north of Strip Pit 4 (= GIS point 157 at 38.09101,-94.44680, beside lot 7815). On the leaf-off frames the northern spot is a gravel pull-off roughly 20 x 10 m on the east side of the gravel road ~140 m in from Route A, in closed woods; the southern one is a smaller roadside gravel widening. These are designated points at small lots, not boat-ramp lots. A 23-ft rig fits the northern lot; it is tight but workable at the southern one. Gravel road off paved Route A, no ford, no 4WD wording.

WATERFRONT (stored not waterfront, kept): the brochure counts 'six water-filled strip-pits totaling 23 acres' - each a narrow trench well under the 5-acre pond line. Strip Pit 1 is ~60 m east of the northern spot and Strip Pit 3/4 ~40 m west of the southern one, both behind continuous timber. No water in view from either spot on leaf-off imagery.
BROCHURE RULES worth knowing: 'No open fires.' and 'Vehicle use is restricted to graveled roadways and parking areas' (Harmony Mission Lake & Peabody brochure). The fire ban is in the note.

CLUSTERS: the two spots are 875 m apart on the same road and entrance - no split. The map's two further camping symbols on SW 9508 belong to Harmony Mission Lake Conservation Area, already entry 13806.
PIN: stored 38.09857,-94.44951 = GIS point 158 at the northern lot - fine.
